meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay, and the zero you gave him.
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess, then. If that's Turnitin, its own guide says the score shouldn't be the sole basis for action against a student, and your procedure says the same thing. What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me why you think Owen didn't write his essay.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend, and pasting a draft in from another file proves nothing about who wrote it. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Editions differ, Hale, and seventeen-year-olds misquote. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, that's what an outline is for. And you've skipped my question about Owen twice now.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
So he was heard, the day before. Those are your own notes about a seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher. What exactly are you proposing, Hale?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home is no comparison at all. You've put five things in front of me and nothing on the table.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

Then Owen does the rewrite, to put this behind him, and nothing more than that. I want a date this week, the new mark entered well before his December 1 scholarship deadline, and every word of 4.4 in that email tonight. Where are you holding it?
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school, then. Where, and who else is in the room?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes, on those terms. Your email tonight names the room and says no one but you is in it with him. And the new mark goes in before December 1, not after.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed in his record. I still require your email to name the room, confirm that no one but you will be present with him, and confirm that the new mark will be entered before December 1. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation of the room, that only you will be there, and the mark entered before December 1; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: Turning the screen to show the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own file, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and telling her the zero stands, because she distrusts software and it confirmed her belief that the school punishes first.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed close to that, showing the essay appearing in two large edits just before midnight on October 28; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer right away with your November 2 conversation and notes instead of leaving her to ask twice while you moved on to the outline.
